ChannelGap.description:
A channel that lost validity while the stream continued (SC-31a).

Vision §28 requires a capture to describe a multi-channel alignment failure, and
a hole between two segments alone is indistinguishable from a channel that was
never enabled over that interval.

cause.description:
`Alignment` when the block that dropped the channel carried `ALIGNMENT`,
`Stream` otherwise (SC-31a).

local.description: Node-local ordinal, allocated by the owning registry.

Gap.description: An interval of missing samples in the stream (SC-30, Vision §28).

link_dropped.description:
How many blocks the link discarded inside the same interval. A block count,
not a sample count: the samples the link lost are `len − lost`, and are
unrecoverable when `lost` is absent. That is a real limit of what a dropped
header can tell us, not an omission (SC-20b, SC-31).

lost.description: What the stream reported losing, when known (SC-13).

GapCause.description:
What the **stream** lost. A closed, derived set (SC-31, decision S16).

What the **link** lost is the separate `link_dropped` count, not a cause, so a
device overflow inside an interval that also lost a block to the link is still
reported as `OverflowRestart` with its sample count, beside a link-drop count of
one. Collapsing the two into a single cause loses the device's own diagnosis.

oneOf.description: `RESTARTED`: a stream restart, as a UHD overflow produces (SC-31, OV-23a).
A per-channel break on a block carrying `ALIGNMENT` (SC-31a).
A jump with no gap flag on a lossy path (SC-31).

`GAP_BEFORE` with `lost` less than the jump on a lossy path and no carry to
explain the difference (SC-31).

stream_lost.description: What the stream itself reported losing.

NodeId.description:
A node in the (future) multi-host deployment. `LOCAL` is the only legal value in v4.0.

Rule: X7 (`00-overview.md`); it qualifies every id of TM-11, SC-6, SB-3 and MA-19.

Segment.description: A contiguous run of valid samples on one channel (SC-30).

TimePoint.description:
An instant: integer ticks in a named clock domain. Never floating-point seconds.

There is deliberately no `PartialOrd`: two points of different domains cannot be
compared at all, and `a < b` silently answering `false` is the bug class this
model exists to prevent (decision T3).

Rule: TM-1, TM-6.

ticks.description: Tick count relative to the domain's origin; a sample index in a SampleClock (TM-10).

description:
What a stream carried, per SampleClock. There is one map per SampleClock: a
block in another domain ends the map, and the Sink starts a new builder (SC-30).

channels.description: The channel count, constant for the map (SC-30a).

end.description: Just past the last sample the map accounts for (SC-30).

first.description: First sample the map accounts for (SC-30).

valid.description: Per channel, the runs of valid samples (SC-14, SC-30).
